title: The Leeward Landfall
premise: Rafael Thornbury, a salvage diver scraping a living off a wreck the navy quietly forbids anyone to name, has spent years staying off every official record. When an earthquake tide opens a sea cave on the leeward coast, she finds inside it the drowned archive of the Meridian Concession, a colonial salvage empire that erased whole crews from history to keep its permits—and its power—alive. Hunted by the concession's heirs and shadowed by the navy, Rafael assembles a found family of divers, archivists, and one defected inspector, and follows the river that fed the cave upstream to its forbidden source: the flooded company town where the original ledgers, and her own grandmother's name among the erased, still wait. In the climax she floods the concession's claim vaults with truth instead of water, trading her invisibility for testimony; the book ends with the permits expiring unclaimed and Rafael's crew diving the wreck openly at last.
about_author: Theo Yarrow is a former commercial diver turned novelist who writes adventure stories about people the maps forget. He lives in a coastal town where the tide charts are considered local literature.

chapters.title: Dead Weight
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. She dives the unnamed navy wreck alone, salvaging brass while dodging patrol boats, establishing her rule of invisibility and her debt-ridden partnership with old deckhand Marisol. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness when she surfaces to an empty harbor.

chapters.title: The Tide That Lied
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. An earthquake swell drains the bay farther than any chart predicts, exposing a cave mouth beneath the cliffs. Against instinct, she enters and finds sealed strongboxes stamped with the Meridian Concession crest. Beat: wonder curdling into dread as she realizes someone will come for this.

chapters.title: Admission Charged
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Local legend-keeper Father Ekwueme tells her the cave 'charges admission': everyone who's entered it has been erased—records, names, even gravestones. He shows her a 1912 crew list with one line burned out. Beat: recognition, because the burned name is her grandmother's.

chapters.title: Permits and Predators
chapters.summary: Inspector Adaeze Okonkwo's POV, newly arrived to audit the concession's expiring permits. She notices Rafael's salvage reports don't match navy records and flags her. Beat: cold institutional menace—the machinery of erasure is still running.

chapters.title: What the Strongbox Kept
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. She cracks a strongbox: not treasure but ledgers—payroll pages proving the concession sent crews into the flooded mine and wrote them off as lost cargo. Beat: fury and grief as history becomes personal.

chapters.title: The Crew You Keep
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. She recruits Marisol, Ekwueme, and disgraced hydrologist Tomas Reyes, who knows the river feeding the cave runs from the forbidden upper valley. Beat: tentative found-family warmth over bad coffee and worse odds.

chapters.title: Navy Business
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. Ordered to bury her audit findings, she instead visits Rafael covertly—not yet ally, not yet enemy. Beat: her first crack of doubt about whose side the law is on.

chapters.title: The Heir Apparent
chapters.summary: Antagonist Cyrus Meridian-Vale's POV. The last concession heir learns of the opened cave and moves to trigger the permit clause that lets him seal the valley permanently. Beat: elegant, entitled menace—he genuinely believes erasure was mercy.

chapters.title: Night Salvage
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A midnight dive to recover more ledgers goes wrong when a concession security boat rams their skiff; Marisol is injured. Beat: guilt—Rafael's secrecy nearly killed her chosen family.

chapters.title: Charts of the Erased
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Cross-referencing river gauges and old payroll dates, he proves the 'lost cargo' were men sent upriver into the mine town. Beat: scholarly obsession becoming moral conviction.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Meridian-Vale buys her debts and offers clean papers and silence—a return to invisibility, guaranteed. Beat: temptation laid bare; invisibility was never safety, only surrender.

chapters.title: Refusal at Low Water
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. She refuses publicly by filing the first ledger page with Okonkwo, burning her anonymity forever. Patrol boats begin shadowing the harbor. Beat: fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Ledger
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. Reading the payroll against her own audit, she finds her predecessor inspectors all signed identical closure memos. She makes a copy and hides it. Beat: quiet defection begins.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The crew sets out by river toward the forbidden source, navigating rapids, checkpoints, and Meridian-Vale's hired boats. Beat: momentum and camaraderie—the family forged under pursuit.

chapters.title: The Drowned Town
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. They reach the source: a reservoir covering the original company town, its church spire breaking the surface. Diving it, Rafael finds the master ledger vault. Beat: awe and sorrow—walking streets where her grandmother walked.

chapters.title: Names in the Vault
chapters.summary: Ekwueme's POV. Inside the vault, the full record: hundreds of erased crew members, including Rafael's grandmother, who survived the mine and testified before being silenced. Beat: grief becoming inheritance.

chapters.title: Seal Order
chapters.summary: Meridian-Vale's POV. With permits hours from expiry, he invokes emergency authority to dynamite the valley gates, drowning the evidence—and the crew. Beat: villainy fully revealed as self-preservation dressed as legacy.

chapters.title: Rising Water
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The climax: as the gates open, the crew races the flood through the mine tunnels to the cave mouth, ledgers strapped to their backs. Marisol's boat work and Okonkwo's arrival stall the demolition crew. Beat: terror, sacrifice, and trust pushed to breaking.

chapters.title: The Testimony
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. At the harbor, with floodwater still surging, she reads the ledgers into the public record as the permits expire, voiding the concession's claims. Meridian-Vale's own signature damns him. Beat: triumph through procedure, not violence.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The valley reopens; families of the erased reclaim names from the restored rolls. Rafael visits her grandmother's reinstated grave. Beat: mourning finally allowed to become peace.

chapters.title: Open Water
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Months later, the crew dives the navy wreck openly under a research permit Okonkwo secured. The wilderness still forgives nothing—but they no longer need forgiveness. Beat: belonging without hiding.

chapters.title: The Leeward Landfall
chapters.summary: Ensemble close, mostly Rafael's POV. On the leeward shore at dawn, the crew buries a time capsule of the recovered ledgers' copies and raises a new flag over the old boathouse. Final beat: memory kept by choice, family kept by practice, power returned to the named.
